permitted_claims: Restart v1 persists committed continuation state and provenance, not arbitrary process memory.
The frozen FMR restart record schema is version 2 and delegates committed-state reconstruction to kernel persistence schema version 1.
A restart bundle carries parameter-set identity; per-column records carry stable column/parameter/template identity, lineage, revision, committed time binding and typed physical continuation state.
Immutable parameter payload, forcing, solver/Newton/Jacobian scratch and worker warm starts are not components of the frozen restart record.
Export is sourced from ready committed state and fails closed on structural/template/state incompatibility.
Restore validates schema, parameter-set identity, template identity, parameter references, physical-state family and uninitialized targets before publication.
Restore is atomic at the runtime registry boundary: candidate committed states are built first and the target registry is assigned only after all records succeed.
Checkpoint/trial orchestration keeps committed checkpoint authority separate from candidate trial state; candidates are explicitly committed or discarded.
The persistence boundary is serialization-neutral and does not define a filesystem or byte format.
forbidden_claims: No mid-transaction trial-state or disposable worker-scratch persistence qualification.
No filesystem or byte-format standardization claim.
No deep-vadose or broad MODFLOW restart qualification.
No parallel/concurrent real-physics MultiSWAP restart claim beyond separately admitted authority.
No new production functionality, physics, numerical policy or restart semantics.
